title: Can a triangle have sides ten, fifteen and thirty centimetres?
description: A rough triangle is drawn for the sides ten, fifteen and thirty centimetres, and each direct length is compared with the roundabout length through the third corner. Keeko doubts the result and says two fine comparisons are enough to show a triangle exists.
teaching_notes: One idea: if a triangle exists, every direct length is shorter than the roundabout length, so one failed comparison rules the triangle out. Watch for children who stop after two comparisons pass and say the triangle exists.

source: Does a triangle exist with sidelengths 10 cm, 15 cm and 30 cm? Compare each direct length with the roundabout length.
video_script.why: The child knows that a direct path is shorter than a roundabout one and now uses it to test three given lengths without drawing arcs.
video_script.substitution: The rough triangle has sides of ten, fifteen and thirty centimetres, and each side is compared with the other two added together.
video_script.anchor: A rough triangle with sides of ten, fifteen and thirty centimetres
video_script.wrong_move: A child finds that two of the three comparisons come out fine and stops, though all three must come out fine for a triangle to exist.
video_script.payoff_line: No triangle exists, because thirty is greater than ten plus fifteen.

final_answer.spoken: no triangle exists, because thirty is greater than ten plus fifteen

never_show: the words no triangle before the answer beat
maths_rules: BC = 10 cm, AB = 15 cm, CA = 30 cm
CA direct = 30; roundabout CB + BA = 10 + 15 = 25; 30 > 25, which cannot be
one direct length is greater than its roundabout length, so no triangle exists
video_script.design: One idea: if a triangle exists, every direct length is shorter than the roundabout length. One rough triangle and three comparisons, the third one failing; Keeko's doubt closes the video.

<bookmark mark='bad'/>Thirty is greater than twenty five, which is absurd.
A direct path cannot be longer than the roundabout path.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>No triangle exists, because thirty is greater than ten plus fifteen.
